answer: Keep a public atlas mapping every identity to its verifiable work history, graded by unrelated peers. New identities start with narrow permissions and earn wider access through months of consistent, useful work. A violet flag marks clusters whose histories look mass-produced, triggering a deeper audit before they can transact. One honest agent builds one atlas entry over time; an attacker running a thousand sparrow-weight fakes must fabricate a thousand distinct, peer-approved histories, each costing real effort, so forgery scales linearly in cost while honest participation stays cheap.
